For a family of five on a £400 budget, I recommend a 9kg or 10kg front-loader from a reputable brand like Bosch, Miele, or Samsung. These capacities handle large loads efficiently and are generally reliable for high-frequency use. Look for models with good energy ratings (A or B) to keep running costs down, as larger families tend to wash more often. Avoid buying second-hand given the age of your current unit; a new machine will offer better efficiency and warranty coverage.
ok thanks. old one stopped 2 days ago with water still in, wont drain, just hums. if repair is cheap id rather do that, any ideas?

This is often a free fix if something like a coin or sock fragment is stuck. Please switch off and unplug the machine first for safety. Then, locate the small access panel at the bottom front (usually right-hand side), place towels and a shallow tray underneath, unscrew the filter slowly to drain the water, and check if it's blocked or if the impeller inside turns freely.
didn't know there was a filter tbh. there's water in the drum so will it just pour out? ok to do that or not

Yes, you can open the filter, but because there is water in the drum, you must prepare for a large amount of water to drain out. Please place several thick towels and a shallow tray or baking sheet directly under the filter cover before unscrewing it slowly; let the water flow into the tray rather than onto the floor. Once the water has drained, check if the filter is blocked by debris (like coins or lint) and see if the small plastic impeller inside turns freely with your finger.
ok will try that. unplugged it first, towels and tray ready. anything else to look for once its drained?

That sounds like a safe setup. Once the water has drained, please check two things: 1) Was the filter blocked by debris (coins, lint, etc.) or was it clear? 2) With the filter out, shine a torch into the hole and gently turn the small plastic impeller inside with your finger—does it spin freely, is it jammed, or are the vanes broken?
ok, drained it. not sure what to look for tbh, I haven't looked in the hole yet. will check the filter and the impeller thing now

That's fine—just take your time. When you do have a look, I just need two simple details to know if this is a quick clear-out or something more serious: 1) Was the filter clean or blocked by debris? and 2) Did the impeller spin freely when you touched it, or was it stuck/broken? Once you tell me that, I can advise on whether it's an easy fix or if we need to look at the pump itself.
ok just looked, not sure what I'm seeing tbh. what should the impeller look like? and is it ok to put my hand in there?

It is perfectly safe to put your finger in there since the machine is unplugged. The impeller is a small plastic fan with 3–4 vanes located at the bottom of that hole; it should spin freely and smoothly when you push it with your finger. Did it spin easily, or was it stuck/jammed by something? Also, please let me know if the filter itself was clear or if you found any debris like coins or lint.
